1:
\textbf{(a)} Disks about the $x$-axis:
\[V=\int_1^5\pi\big(e^{-x^2}\big)^2dx=\int_1^5\pi e^{-2x^2}dx.\]
\textbf{(b)} $\Delta x=1$, nodes $1,\dots,5$, $g(x)=\pi e^{-2x^2}$:
\[S_4=\frac13\Big[g(1)+4g(2)+2g(3)+4g(4)+g(5)\Big]=\frac\pi3\Big[e^{-2}+4e^{-8}+2e^{-18}+4e^{-32}+e^{-50}\Big]\approx\boxed{0.14}.\]
(The true value is about $0.09$: Simpson's rule with $n=4$ is coarse here because the integrand drops so fast.)
2:
\textbf{(a)} Let $w=\tan^{-1}x$, $dw=\frac{dx}{1+x^2}$:
\[\int\ln w\,dw=w\ln w-w+C=\boxed{\tan^{-1}x\,\ln(\tan^{-1}x)-\tan^{-1}x+C}.\]
\textbf{(b)} Let $u=\sin2x$, $du=2\cos2x\,dx$, $u$ from $-1$ to $1$:
\[\frac12\int_{-1}^1\sqrt{4-u^2}\,du=\frac12\Big[\frac u2\sqrt{4-u^2}+2\sin^{-1}\frac u2\Big]_{-1}^1=\frac12\Big[\sqrt3+\frac{2\pi}{3}\Big]=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+\frac\pi3}.\]
4:
\textbf{(a)} $x'=-e^{-t}\cos4\pi t-4\pi e^{-t}\sin4\pi t$ and $y'=-e^{-t}\sin4\pi t+4\pi e^{-t}\cos4\pi t$. The cross terms cancel:
\[(x')^2+(y')^2=e^{-2t}(1+16\pi^2),\qquad L=\int_0^\infty\sqrt{1+16\pi^2}\,e^{-t}\,dt.\]
\textbf{(b)} It converges: $\sqrt{1+16\pi^2}\lim_{T\to\infty}\big[-e^{-t}\big]_0^T=\boxed{\sqrt{1+16\pi^2}}\approx12.61$.
5:
Measure $y$ up from the tip. By similar triangles the radius at height $y$ is $\frac y2$. A slice has volume $\pi\frac{y^2}{4}dy$ and is lifted $2-y$ m:
\[W=\int_0^29800\pi\frac{y^2}{4}(2-y)\,dy=2450\pi\Big[\frac{2y^3}{3}-\frac{y^4}{4}\Big]_0^2=2450\pi\cdot\frac43=\frac{9800\pi}{3}\approx\boxed{10262.5\ \text{J}}.\]
